title: Redwood discovery - model selection - Vela Systems

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-10
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Nguyen (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (CTO - Vela Systems), Liam O'Connor (Lead ML Eng), Aisha Malik (Security), Noah Kim (Product)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood intro, ask about current stack and pain points. Vela needs long context for support tickets, multilingual support across EN/FR/ES/DE, and tool-calling into their Jira-like ticketing system. Talks about tradeoffs between latency and cost and asks about Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployments. Security questions about SOC2, KMS, SSO. Agreement to run benchmarks.

Transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia Nguyen, I'm the AE on this account, and I have Carlos from our SE team with me. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Priya (Vela): Good thanks, thanks for taking the time. We're excited to talk through model selection, we have a few constraints to share.
[00:15] Carlos (Redwood): Hey all, quick agenda — we'll do a quick discovery on requirements, current infra, and then talk about model options (open models, context length, multilingual) and hosting options.
[00:26] Liam (Vela): Quick context: we run a support assistant that ingests full ticket threads, sometimes 15+ messages, plus attachments. Our current prompt windows get truncated; we need at least 32k tokens of context to avoid losing conversation history. We also need multilingual support primarily EN/FR/ES/DE.
[00:40] Aisha (Vela): From security — we have strict data residency and KMS requirements; we'd like to know if Redwood can do private deployment in our VPC or on-prem.
[00:50] Sofia: Great, that aligns with a lot we've seen. For 32k context we typically look at larger open models or configured variants; we support hosted, dedicated, and private modes. There's tradeoffs — latency and cost vary by model and deployment.
[01:05] Carlos: For model choices, open models we commonly recommend for this are: Llama-3 (community builds), Mistral-Instruct variants, and some of the 32k-context forks (we also have Redwood-verified builds). Note: transcription might say "Lama3" sometimes in auto text. Llama-3 sometimes called Lama in older notes.
[01:26] Liam: Are those models tool-calling capable? We need function-calling to trigger actions in our ticketing system and to call a KB retriever.
[01:33] Carlos: Short answer: yes, we support structured tool-calling patterns. For hosted API we surface function-calling primitives and streaming; for Dedicated/Private we can expose the same APIs behind your VPC with local connectors to your systems. Implementation detail: we usually wire a small adapter that takes model output and maps to your ticketing API.
[01:55] Priya: On latency — we target sub-400ms token latency for short replies, but longer generations are fine as long as interactive agents feel snappy. How does context length affect that?
[02:06] Carlos: Big impact. With 32k context, memory and KV cache grows; throughput per GPU drops and you see higher per-token latency generally. We mitigate with prefix caching and batching; for low-latency we often suggest Dedicated pools sized for your QPS and pinning model variants.
[02:26] Aisha: And encryption in transit and at rest? KMS?
[02:29] Sofia: Yes, Hosted supports customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) for enterprise tiers, Dedicated and Private give you more control — Private can use your HSM/KMS and stay inside your VPC. We'll share our SOC 2 and network architecture doc after the call.
[02:45] Noah (Vela): Do you have concrete numbers on cost differences Hosted vs Dedicated for an 8k vs 32k workload? I'm trying to model TCO.
[02:53] Sofia: We have a TCO spreadsheet we can share. Roughly, Hosted is pay-as-you-go and can be cheaper for intermittent traffic, but Dedicated offers lower per-token costs at steady high throughput. For 32k context you may need more memory per machine or use quantized weights; Dedicated lets you tune that and reserve capacity for SLOs.
[03:16] Liam: Multilingual — which models perform best for FR/ES/DE? We saw some drop-off on French in Llama-2 in our tests.
[03:24] Carlos: Mistral variants and some European-focused checkpoints tend to do well, but it's workload-dependent. We recommend running evals on your sample tickets. Redwood Optimize can run per-language quality comparisons and recommend quantization or model switches by language.
[03:45] Priya: If we go private (on-prem), what's the timeline and support level?
[03:50] Sofia: Private takes longer; typical on-prem pilot is 6-10 weeks including security review, network setup, and model onboarding. Dedicated in your cloud VPC can be faster — 2-4 weeks. Hosted is immediate for proofs-of-concept.
[04:06] Aisha: For audits, will you provide logs and traceability?
[04:09] Carlos: Yes, audit logs, per-route tracing, and token-level usage are available. We can push logs to your SIEM if needed.
[04:20] Priya: Ok, concrete next steps — we want a benchmark with 8k and 32k contexts, run across 3 candidate models, and want to see latency, cost, and per-language accuracy.
[04:31] Sofia: Perfect — we'll put together a benchmark plan. Carlos will lead the technical plan and we'll need sample data from you.
[04:38] Liam: A couple of gotchas: attachments — we often strip or summarize PDFs before sending to the model; any suggestions?
[04:43] Carlos: We recommend a two-step pipeline: extractor -> vectorize/summarize -> include summary in prompt. For very long attachments, store in KB and use retrieval augmented generation (RAG). We can demo a connector for your KB.
[04:58] Priya: Any proprietary models or Redwood-specific optimizations we should consider?
[05:02] Sofia: We don't force proprietary models; we curate open models and provide verified performance profiles and runtime optimizations (kernel selection, quantization paths, prefix caching). For some customers we recommend Redwood-verified builds tuned for long context.
[05:20] Noah: What about function-calling reliability — we can't have hallucinations leading to ticket changes incorrectly.
[05:27] Carlos: We recommend explicit structured schemas for actions, validation steps, and an approval step in critical flows. Also we can run model-level calibrations and prompt engineering to reduce hallucinations. For dedicated deployments, you can run deterministic decoders if that helps.
[05:50] Priya: From compliance — what about data residency in EU? Some of our data must stay in eu-west-1.
[05:56] Sofia: We support regional routing. Hosted can pin region; Dedicated and Private give you full control. We'll note that for the TCO.
[06:05] Aisha: SSO — we need SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[06:09] Sofia: Yes, enterprise tiers have SAML SSO, SCIM user provisioning, and RBAC. We'll include that in the docs.
[06:20] Liam: For the benchmark, what models do you suggest we test first?
[06:24] Carlos: Suggestion: 1) Mistral-Instruct 8k (good baseline), 2) Llama-3-family 32k variant (open forks or community builds), 3) Redwood-verified 32k tuned build (if available). We'll include quantized variants for cost comparison.
[06:42] Priya: Do you support streaming responses for partial replies? That helps UX even if token latency is higher.
[06:47] Carlos: Yes, streaming is supported across hosted and dedicated. Private can be configured to stream too.
[06:53] Sofia: Ok quick recap — actions: we'll send TCO/pricing, SOC2 and network docs, and a benchmark plan. Vela will send sample tickets and requirements. Pilot timeline TBD but aiming for mid-March kickoff.
[07:08] Priya: Sounds good. One more — for Dedicated sizing, do you give recommendations based on QPS and average length?
[07:13] Carlos: Yes, we'll run a sizing exercise — need your expected peak QPS, average tokens per request, and desired latency SLOs. We'll include that in the benchmark doc.
[07:25] Noah: Can Redwood's KV cache be shared across a dedicated pool or is it per-instance?
[07:30] Carlos: KV cache is per-session/instance but our runtime supports warm caches and prefix caching policies so repeated prefixes hit cache; for Dedicated we can pin sessions to instances to improve hit rates.
[07:42] Aisha: For legal, we'll need a DPA and data processing terms.
[07:46] Sofia: We'll share our DPA and legal templates.
[07:51] Priya: Alright thanks everyone, looking forward to the benchmark.
[07:54] Sofia: Thanks — Carlos will follow up on the technical plan. We'll send the docs and proposed dates.

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription had some brand/model name swaps (e.g., Llama -> Lama), and occasional speaker attribution glitches.

End of call.
